title: Teriyaki Chicken
subtitle: Glazed pan-fried chicken thighs with a sweet soy sauce
excerpt: Teriyaki is a technique as much as a recipe: the sugar in the sauce caramelises in the pan and gives the chicken its lacquered, glossy finish. Chicken thighs suit it better than breast because they stay juicy even when the sauce is reduced around them.
sourceNotes: Teriyaki is a Japanese cooking technique in which food is grilled or pan-fried with a glaze of soy sauce, mirin, and sugar. The word combines teri, meaning lustre, with yaki, meaning grill or fry. The technique is several centuries old, though its global popularity is more recent.

content.text: Cook the chicken first until almost done, then add the sauce and let it reduce around the meat. Adding the sauce too early means it burns before the chicken is cooked through.
Mix together the soy sauce, mirin, honey, garlic, and ginger in a small bowl to make the teriyaki sauce.
Heat the sesame oil in the frying pan over medium heat. Add the chicken thighs smooth-side down and cook for 6-7 minutes until deeply golden.
Flip the chicken and cook for a further 5 minutes until cooked through. If the thighs are thick, check by cutting into the thickest part -- the juices should run clear.
Pour the teriyaki sauce into the pan. It will bubble immediately. Spoon it over the chicken continuously for 2-3 minutes as it reduces to a thick glaze.
Remove from the heat and rest the chicken for 2 minutes. Slice and serve over rice, spooning any remaining glaze over the top. Scatter with spring onion.

items.cause: Heat too high when the sauce was added.
items.fix: Reduce the heat to medium-low before adding the sauce and keep spooning it over the chicken rather than leaving it to sit.
